bug_semantics: CWE-400/CWE-770 DoS in @adonisjs/bodyparser PartHandler file-type detection: while MultipartFile.extname is still undefined, reportProgress concatenates every incoming multipart chunk into an in-memory detection buffer and re-runs magic-number detection. After the bound was dropped, getFileType returned null for the entire streaming path whenever content did not match a known signature (force=false on every chunk), so the buffer grew with the upload instead of stopping around file-type.minimumBytes (~4100). With deferred validations or a permissive size limit the stream is never short-circuited, and a public multipart endpoint can be crashed by a large or unbounded part whose body is not a known magic type (e.g. a fake .png of 0x41 bytes).
flaw_origin: On 2020-02-08 Harminder Virk upgraded file-type to its async fromBuffer API in 7bc00981abe82ee5cd87121edcce4c121256dd83. The parent still returned null only while fileContents.length < fileType.minimumBytes && !force, then fell back to the client filename/Content-Type. The upgrade replaced that predicate with if (!force) return null, while PartHandler.reportProgress continued to call detectFileTypeAndExtension(false) and Buffer.concat until extname was set. That is the first public write of unbounded type-detection buffering; later 0740a35f46ea48204db3c391f82affe7699b3ce2 moved fallback out of getFileType and d7132493de91cbf23f572f5762219b30e6067f60 extended magic inspection to extensionless names, but both are refinements of this mechanism, not a smaller first-write.

reasoning: Vulnerability-first: GHSA-xx9g-fh25-4q64 / CVE-2026-25762 is a published (not withdrawn/rejected) DoS in @adonisjs/bodyparser multipart handling. PartHandler keeps a detection buffer while extname is undefined; magic-number getFileType can fail forever on non-matching content; with deferred validations or a large size limit the process allocates until OOM. Pre-2020 the same concat loop was bounded because getFileType fell back to the filename after file-type.minimumBytes (~4100) even with force=false. The smallest commit that first wrote the unbounded streaming path is 7bc00981abe82ee5cd87121edcce4c121256dd83, which dropped that length check while reportProgress still invoked detection with force=false. Direct parent-tree check at 82a5d3b06bb05d198d7ab88b241f8067a4ccfb80 shows the minimumBytes predicate and filename fallback still present, so introducer_parent_absent=true. The commit is a single-parent regular object (not a merge, move, revert, or reconstructable squash). It precedes the affected tags (first in v3.2.1; in v10.1.2 and v11.0.0-next.8) and both patched tags land the 4100-byte fallback after the affected boundary. Later 0740a35/d713249/43946d1 preserved or renamed the sink and are not BICs.
